title: 11D Projection / Information / Symmetry Unification — Older Research Recovery
status: library deep-research archaeology + mathematical reconstruction programme; mixed standard and speculative elements; original date unresolved
source_class: older deep-research report recovered from Library; not automatically primary Tim-authored notation
abstract: This record reconstructs an older project attempt to treat eleven-dimensional structure, lower-dimensional descriptions, symmetry reduction and information preservation within one mathematical language. Its strongest scientific interpretation is not that reality literally moves up and down a numbered ladder of dimensions, but that different descriptions may be related by projection, coarse-graining, embedding and reconstruction maps whose information loss can be quantified. The core problem is therefore an inverse problem: given a higher-dimensional state X, a projection pi_d(X) and a proposed reconstruction R_d, what features of X are recoverable, what invariants survive, and which distinctions are irretrievably lost? A serious version requires an explicit 11D geometry or field configuration, a measure/probability structure, physically motivated projection or compactification maps, symmetry representations, a reconstruction loss and an observable correspondence to four-dimensional physics. Category theory, topology, mutual information and Kaluza-Klein/M-theory machinery can then be used as tools, but none supplies the missing physical derivation automatically. The model is currently T2: valuable as a rigorous architecture for multi-description systems and compactification questions, but not yet a unique or experimentally specified 11D theory.
research_question: Under what explicit geometric, dynamical and information-theoretic conditions can an 11D state be reduced to lower-dimensional effective descriptions while retaining reconstructible structure, and can any nontrivial invariant be proved to survive the reduction?
importance: This predates the September SU(4)/SU(5) extension as a broader group-theoretic unification route: dimensions, projections, Lie groups, supersymmetry, topology, holography and information were already being assembled into one mathematical architecture.
maturity: T2 mathematical architecture; no unique physical compactification or experimental prediction selected

minimal_solvable_research_program.goal: Turn the broad 11D idea into one explicit inverse problem before attempting a full physical unification.
steps: Choose a concrete state space P and reduction map pi.
Specify a probability measure or dataset on P if information quantities are used.
Define reconstruction R and a loss d.
Compute the irreducible reconstruction error and identify sufficient variables for the chosen task.
Identify exact symmetries/topological invariants of the model and prove which are preserved by pi/R.
If the model is physical spacetime, replace the generic projection with an explicit compactification/dimensional reduction and derive the 4D spectrum.
Only after that compare the derived low-dimensional theory with observations.

falsification_and_failure_conditions: A proposed invariant I* fails if explicit allowed states with different I* values map into one another under the claimed dimension-changing operation.
A reconstruction claim fails if multiple admissible high-dimensional states map to the same lower state and no additional information resolves the degeneracy.
A physical compactification proposal fails if it cannot produce a consistent 4D effective spectrum/dynamics or violates relevant observations.
A purported unification remains merely organizational if group names and dimension labels do not determine couplings, representations and observables.
important_corrections: The old report's G5=SO(4,1) as an AdS5 isometry is incorrect: AdS5 has isometry SO(4,2).

A six-real-dimensional Calabi-Yau threefold is a standard 10D->4D string compactification comparator; direct 11D->4D minimal supersymmetry instead naturally points to a seven-real-dimensional G2-holonomy space.
E8 or E8xE8 is an internal gauge/algebraic structure in specific string/M-theory constructions, not an alternative to the 11D Lorentz group SO(10,1) as a spacetime symmetry.
OSp(1|32) is useful in historical/algebraic discussions of 11D supersymmetry but should not be labeled simply 'the M-theory symmetry group'.
Noether conservation follows from continuous symmetries of an action; a cross-dimensional I* does not follow automatically from the existence of projection maps.
A projection pi_d is generally information-losing and need not possess an inverse or satisfy pi o R=id unless explicit section/reconstruction conditions are imposed.
research_value: The strongest contribution of this model is a precise cross-description problem: projection, information loss, reconstruction, invariants and hidden fibers. That architecture can be used in real mathematics, dimensional reduction, machine learning or data compression even if the physical 11D interpretation is never established.
provenance_boundary: The recovered report itself classified physical/theological mappings as metaphorical/mathematical rather than experimentally demonstrated. Preserve that boundary.
